name: area_scales_with_the_square_of_the_height
why: The area of the letters cannot be predicted from the string -- it depends on the font -- but it goes with the SQUARE of the height, and that, yes, can be demanded. Doubling the height quadruples the area: two different measurements that check each other, and neither is a hand-written constant that someone will one day update to the wrong number.
_why_this_is_the_law_that_exposes_the_cu: It is the finest check there is in here. Measured before writing the operation: 5 mm -> 1.1533; 10 mm -> 1.1535; 20 mm -> 0.6647. The third number is not a font misbehaving: it is «PROVA» at 20 mm that is 94 mm wide and does not fit on the 100 face, anchored where it was -- half of the letters had disappeared and the ratio said so. Here the heights all fit inside, and the ratio must come out equal: if one day it did not, it would mean something is being cut away in silence.
_why_from_the_third_step_on_n_is_needed: ENGRAVING MULTIPLIES THE FACES. After the first inscription the forward-facing faces are TEN, not one: the bottom of each letter is a new face with the same normal, and the bench refuses to guess which is the right one. «n=1» means «the largest», which is the starting face: the others are the bottoms of the letters, a few square millimetres wide. It is a choice, and it is written down.

expect.tolerance_why: exact half of the width at 10 mm: the box goes LINEARLY with the height, and it is the first of the two facts that hold up the second
the area is the sum of 56 tessellated curved outlines; at 5 mm the outlines are small and the relative noise is the highest of the three
it is a ratio between two numbers that already carry tolerance: a hundredth is less than 1% and is much narrower than the half that would separate this case from a cut-off inscription
the double of the above, for the same reason
four times the one at 5 mm, and with four times the absolute noise

expect.why: THE SAME NUMBER AS THE HALF-HEIGHT INSCRIPTION. This line is the proof: the two engravings have volumes that differ by four times, and the ratio is the same to the third digit.
half a millimetre is the real marking, the one put on a part to be delivered: the other two are deep to make the numbers add up, not because one would engrave that way

expect.tolerance_why: at 3 mm of height and half a millimetre of depth the removed volume is under 6 mm3, and the tessellation noise weighs double
expect.why: THE RATIO DOES NOT DEPEND ON THE DEPTH. If it did, the operation would be dividing by the wrong number -- and nobody would notice as long as all the engravings are equally deep.
